problems.title: Latency ladder
problems.solution: Roughly 1 ns, 80–100 ns, 1–5 µs. Know these to within 2×.

problems.title: Cache lines
problems.solution: 62,500 lines, 16 ints each, streamed by the prefetcher.

problems.title: Bandwidth vs latency
problems.statement: 10⁸ elements. Vector sum at 20 GB/s with 4-byte ints vs a shuffled linked list at 90 ns per dependent miss.

problems.title: TLB reach
problems.solution: 6 MB vs 3 GB. That's why huge pages help random access over large tables.

problems.title: Page faults
problems.statement: malloc(1 GB) and then touching every byte once.

parts.prompt: Why does malloc itself return fast?
options: pages are mapped lazily on first touch

problems.solution: 262,144 faults at roughly 0.5–1 µs each, a quarter of a second. Pre-fault (touch or MAP_POPULATE) before latency-critical work.

problems.title: NUMA
problems.statement: A thread on socket 0 reads a buffer that a thread on socket 1 initialised.

options: initialise on the node that will use it, or bind with numactl / mbind

problems.title: AoS vs SoA
problems.statement: 10⁷ particles of {x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, mass, id} (8 × 8 bytes); a loop reads only mass.

parts.prompt: Bytes pulled through the cache with AoS (MB)?

hints: A whole line per particle vs a contiguous mass array.
problems.solution: 640 MB vs 80 MB: 8× less traffic for SoA.

problems.title: Memory-level parallelism
problems.statement: Walking 8 independent shuffled lists in an interleaved loop vs one at a time (90 ns misses, the core sustains ~10 outstanding misses).
problems.solution: About 8×: the 8 dependent chains proceed in parallel, limited by the miss-handling resources.
